cues.en: Journals are private companies owned by traditional book publishers or subsidized by universities and science foundations. The journals themselves don't do research. Scientists from relevant fields send in manuscripts according to the guidelines set out by the journals. The journals employ editors who have backgrounds in the scientific fields. They do a first screening of papers which filters out the bulk of submissions and the ones they think are interesting and worthy of publishing they then send out to more experienced professionals in the field working at universities or similar labs. This is where the peer in peer review comes from. The reviewers don't work for the journal. They're working for free and anonymously
cues.zh: 期刊是私营公司，要么归传统图书出版商所有，要么由大学和科学基金会资助。期刊本身并不做研究。相关领域的科学家会按照期刊制定的规范提交稿件。期刊会聘用具有相关学科背景的编辑。他们先对论文进行初筛，过滤掉绝大部分投稿，然后将他们认为有价值、值得发表的论文，送交至大学或类似实验室里更有经验的同行手中。这就是“同行评审”中“同行”一词的由来。审稿人并不受雇于期刊。他们完全是匿名且免费提供劳务的，

cues.en: by writing valuable comments and critiques that they then send back to the editors who then relay those back to the original researchers for changes. This stressful tennis match goes back and forth for a few weeks to a couple months and the paper either gets published or it gets rejected. Journals serve an important and necessary function by sharing scientific advancements with the rest of the world under a consistent set of standards. Publishing is not a quick process and nor is it an easy one. It's absolutely not a perfect system though don't get me wrong. At the end of the day journals are still a business which is why you usually need to shell out $15 a paper if you don't attend or work for a university.
cues.zh: 撰写有价值的审稿意见和批评，再反馈给编辑，最后由编辑转达给原作者进行修改。这场让人心力交瘁的拉锯战会来回持续几周到几个月，论文最终要么成功发表，要么被拒。期刊通过一套统一的标准向全世界分享科研进展，发挥着至关重要且不可或缺的作用。发表绝不是一个快速的过程，也绝非易事。不过别误会，这套机制绝谈不上完美。归根结底，期刊终究是一门生意，这也是为什么如果你不在大学就读或任职，通常看一篇论文就得自掏腰包花上 15 美元。

cues.zh: 这数字听起来可能不算多，尤其是我们习惯了动辄上百万的转发量和订阅数。但你可以这么想：每一次引用都来自一项原创研究，由团队耗时数月、甚至数年完成、写成论文，再通过期刊评审流程。亨德里克打破了有机物的壁垒。现在有了能与硅匹敌的可行半导体

To this day this is still Hendrik's most cited paper and he took advantage of the hype to pump out several more papers on whatever organic crystal his buddy Clock had been playing with that week. But Hendrik seemed to recognize that swapping out pentacene for a new organic crystal was gonna get old at some point and the community would lose interest. So he went several steps beyond. He had invented the world's

cues.en: It seemed like every new crystal he touched had untapped potential no one had seen before. He didn't stop there though. Not long after he published a paper on the quantum hall effect. The quantum hall effect is an obscure phenomenon where the resistivity climbs in a discrete staircase effect like you can see here. It's observed only temperatures close to absolute zero because you've removed all the thermal noise from the system and you're quite literally observing the flow of individual electrons.
cues.zh: 他经手的每一块新晶体，似乎都藏着前所未见的潜力。但他并未止步于此。不久后，他又发表了一篇关于量子霍尔效应的论文。量子霍尔效应是一种晦涩的物理现象，电阻率会像大家看到的这样呈离散的阶梯状上升。这种现象只有在接近绝对零度时才能观察到，因为此时排除了系统中所有的热噪声，你实际上就是在观测单个电子的流动。

cues.en: Again by demonstrating it in organics Hendrik had claimed to another first for physics. When Hendrik signed on to Bell Labs, Betlog was already getting up in years. cues.en: After Bettlag had left Bell Labs for good Hendrik continued to work on the crystals provided to him by clock but began collaborating with some chemists in France as well. But it was his collaboration with Bell Labs chemist Ynon Bao which would prove to be his boldest but also final performance.
cues.zh: Bettlag 永久离开 Bell Labs 后，Hendrik 继续研究 clock 提供给他的晶体，但也开始与法国的一些化学家合作。不过，正是他与 Bell Labs 化学家 Ynon Bao 的合作，后来证明是他最大胆、也是最后的绝唱。

cues.en: On paper you can just make transistors smaller and and smaller. Pack more and more into the same space and computing power should keep increasing. But in reality silicon can't be miniaturized past a certain point. Power density doesn't scale down alongside the transistor so you're still pumping the same number of watts per unit area and with your transistors packed so tightly you get current leakage and overheating. It means at our current pace of silicon Moore's law is going to fail.
cues.zh: 理论上，你可以把晶体管越做越小。在同样空间里塞进越来越多，算力就应该持续增长。但现实中，硅的微缩有极限。功率密度不会随晶体管一起缩小，所以单位面积仍在输入同样的瓦数；晶体管排得太密，就会漏电和过热。这意味着按当前硅的发展速度，摩尔定律将会失效。

In July 2000 along with Bettlag and Klock he shared a $10,000

cues.zh: 事情过去二十年后，很难追溯传闻的来源；但如果要我猜关于 Hendrik 获诺贝尔奖的热议从何而来，

cues.en: In 2002 it seemed like Hendrik was considering leaving Bell Labs behind. As well as being under consideration for a professorship at Princeton, he was near to getting an offer from the Max Planck Institute back in Germany. Hendrik would have been the youngest person ever to receive a full research directorship there.
cues.zh: 2002 年，Hendrik 似乎在考虑离开 Bell Labs。除了有望拿到 Princeton 的教职，他还几乎拿到了德国 Max Planck Institute 的录用通知。如果成真，Hendrik 将成为该机构有史以来最年轻的正研究主任。
